findings_qualitative.value: First detection of the 84 GHz Class I CH3OH maser toward Sgr B2 and first interferometric map of the 5.29 GHz CH2NH maser toward Sgr B2(N).

evidence.quote: We report the first detection of the Class I methanol (CH 3 OH) maser at 84 GHz and the first interferometric map of the methanimine (CH 2 NH) maser at 5.29 GHz toward this region.

findings_qualitative.value: The 5.29 GHz CH2NH maser at 83 km s^-1 is spatially and kinematically coherent with the 84 GHz Class I CH3OH maser toward the K6 H II region (MS2), indicating a collisional pumping mechanism for CH2NH.

evidence.quote: We found that MS2, superimposed on the K6 H II region, harbors maser emission of both Class I CH 3 OH at 84 GHz and CH 2 NH at 5 . 29 GHz (Figure 11).

Their consistent morphology serves as strong evidence to support a similar collisional pumping mechanism for the CH 2 NH maser with the Class I CH 3 OH maser as well as a common physical condition for triggering these masers.

findings_qualitative.value: The 95 GHz CH3OH 8_0 - 7_1 A-type transition shows weaker emission toward the 84 GHz maser spots and is concentrated toward the N1 hot core, similar to thermal molecular lines.

evidence.quote: In contrast, we found that the 95 GHz line exhibits weaker emission toward the identified maser spots in Sgr B2(N) compared to the 84 GHz line. The spatial distribution for the 95 GHz emission is similar to that for other thermal molecular lines, concentrating toward the N1 mm-wave source.

findings_qualitative.value: Masing clumps of CH3OH and CH2NH reside in the colder, lower-density external envelope of Sgr B2(N) (Tk ~ 29-37 K, nH2 ~ (5-8) x 10^4 cm^-3) rather than in the hot cores.

evidence.quote: The relatively low values of temperatures and densities indicate that the masing clumps are situated in the colder and low-density external envelope.

claims.hypothesis: Observed bright emission of CH3OH at 84 GHz (MS1 and MS2) and CH2NH at 5.29 GHz (MS2) toward Sgr B2(N) originates from weak astronomical masers rather than thermal excitation.
claims.experiment: Image 84 GHz CH3OH with ALMA and 5.29 GHz CH2NH with VLA, measure brightness temperatures and morphologies, and perform non-LTE radiative transfer and MCMC spectral fitting.
claims.result: Observed brightness temperatures (>120 K, reaching 389.2 K at MS1) far exceed derived kinetic temperatures (~29-37 K), spectral profiles deviate from LTE, and fitted excitation temperatures and optical depths are negative (tau = -2.44 to -2.52 for CH3OH; tau = -0.03 to -0.006 for CH2NH).
claims.finding: The 84 GHz CH3OH emission toward MS1 and MS2 and 5.29 GHz CH2NH emission toward MS2 are confirmed to be weak masers.

evidence.quote: In contrast, as summarized in Table 2, the observed T B values of the molecular emission investigated in this work ( > 120 K) are significantly higher than the physical temperatures.
All combine to support the observed emission of CH 3 OH at 84 GHz toward both MS1 and MS2 and CH 2 NH at 5.29 GHz toward MS2 to consist of astronomical (weak) masers.

claims.hypothesis: Intense 84 GHz CH3OH Class I maser emission toward MS1, where compact continuum background radiation is absent, can be explained by a two-chain-clump amplification model along the line of sight.
claims.experiment: Fit four E-type CH3OH transitions toward MS1 using a single-clump model versus a two-chained-clump non-LTE radiative transfer model in molsim with MCMC.
claims.result: A single-clump model requires strong background continuum that produces unphysical absorption at 85.5 and 108.9 GHz, whereas the two-chain-clump model (in both single-maser and double-maser scenarios) reproduces both the 84.5 GHz maser and optically thick emission features with weak continuum (Tcont ~ 3.3-3.4 K).
claims.finding: A two-chain-clump self-amplification or background-emission amplification model explains the bright 84 GHz CH3OH maser toward the dark continuum region MS1.

evidence.quote: The results suggest a two-chain-clump model for explaining the intense CH 3 OH Class I maser emission toward a region with low continuum background radiation.

evidence.loc: 4.1.1. Masers with Dark Continuum Background – MS1
evidence.quote: In both scenarios, this model can account for the strong maser emission with an absence of a bright and compact continuum source.

claims.hypothesis: The 5.29 GHz CH2NH maser shares a collisional pumping mechanism with the 84 GHz Class I CH3OH maser.
claims.experiment: Compare the interferometric spatial distribution and velocity structure of the 5.29 GHz CH2NH maser, 84 GHz Class I CH3OH maser, and known radiatively pumped masers (OH, Class II CH3OH), and analyze their energy-level decay and collision propensities.
claims.result: The 83 km s^-1 component of the 5.29 GHz CH2NH maser is spatially and kinematically coincident with the 84 GHz Class I CH3OH maser at MS2 (K6 H II region), offset from radiatively pumped masers, and both molecules show strong intra-stack collisional propensity (Delta K = 0 / |Delta Ka| = 0) feeding metastable levels.
claims.finding: The 5.29 GHz CH2NH maser is collisionally pumped under similar physical conditions (Tk ~ 30 K, nH2 > 5 x 10^4 cm^-3) as the 84 GHz Class I CH3OH maser.

evidence.quote: By comparing the spatial origin and extent of maser emission from several molecular species, we find that the 5.29 GHz CH 2 NH maser has a close spatial relationship with the 84 GHz CH 3 OH Class I masers. This relationship serves as observational evidence to suggest a similar collisional pumping mechanism for these maser transitions.

Their consistent morphology serves as strong evidence to support a similar collisional pumping mechanism for the CH 2 NH maser with the Class I CH 3 OH maser as well as a common physical condition for triggering these masers.

why_this_data.value: Single-dish PRIMOS observations had a large ~2.5' x 2.5' field of view at C band that blended Sgr B2 North and Main, so interferometric VLA and ALMA observations were needed to spatially disentangle the maser components.

evidence.quote: However, the large ∼ 2 . 5 ′ × 2 . 5 ′ field of view of PRIMOS at C band ( ∼ 5 GHz) includes both the North and Main components of Sgr B2, complicating the interpretation of the spectral profiles. Therefore, it is crucial to have interferometric observations to disentangle in detail the various possible spatial components of maser emission.

why_this_method.value: MCMC sampling with a multi-component modified RADEX code explores a larger parameter space more efficiently than least-squares fitting and yields full posterior probability distributions to assess parameter covariances.

evidence.quote: One of the advantages of the MCMC technique over a traditional least-squares fit approach is that a larger parameter space can be explored more efficiently.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single-clump LTE (thermal) model: rejected because observed brightness temperatures (>120 K) far exceed kinetic temperatures (~29-37 K) and spectral profiles deviate substantially from a thermal model.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, we also performed a spectral analysis assuming a single excitation temperature to equal T k for comparison and found that the observed spectral profiles deviate substantially from the thermal model.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Single-clump non-LTE maser model for MS1: rejected because strong background continuum needed to stimulate the 84.5 GHz maser introduces unphysical absorption features at 85.5 and 108.9 GHz and no compact continuum source is observed toward MS1.

how_they_decided_enough.value: Used 100 walkers with 10,000 samples each for MS2 (and 50,000 samples each for MS1 where RADEX convergence slowed down at high Ncol) until parameters converged to well-defined peaks.

evidence.quote: We found that the convergence rate of the RADEX algorithm slows down tremendously at high N col > 10 17 cm − 2 . Therefore, we capped N col at 10 17 . 5 cm − 2 and used 50,000 samples per walker (five times the value used for MS2).

limitations_admitted.value: One-zone escape probability approximation in RADEX/molsim neglects maser beaming, inhomogeneities, and non-local radiative transfer effects, which become significant when optical depth tau < -1 (as in the 84 GHz CH3OH maser where |tau| ~ 2.5).

evidence.quote: Geometric effects related to the propagation of maser radiation become increasingly significant as the optical depth becomes lower than -1. Although RADEX and MOLSIM support various geometries through escape probability approximation, other effects such as maser beaming are not treated.

The models also assume homogeneous physical conditions (i.e. one-zone models), which is inappropriate for very negative optical depths. For precisely modeling maser lines with strong amplification, a non-local treatment of radiation and level population is required.

referee_caveats_inferred: For CH3OH at MS1 and MS2, the derived optical depth is tau ~ -2.44 to -2.52, where maser saturation, beaming, and non-local radiative transfer effects can substantially alter level populations compared to the local escape probability approximation.
The VLA beam (~3.4'' x 1.3'') and ALMA beam (~2.2'' x 1.7'') are not matched in uv-coverage or convolved to a common resolution before extracting spectra toward MS2.
